root_idea.summary: The root centers on one thing being above or upon another.
root_idea.development: From this orientation develop mounting and riding, embarking, placing parts together, layered arrangements, and terms for mounts and mounted groups.

senses.definition: To mount or ride; to embark in or on a vessel.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for being upon an animal and, by extension, for going aboard a ship or traveling upon the sea.

senses.definition: To assemble, compose, or constitute by putting parts or elements together.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, it describes the forming or constituting of a person; the lexical construction also includes fixing one component into another.

senses.definition: Layered, overlapping, or clustered with parts one upon another.
senses.usage_conditions: An active-participial adjective describing an arrangement in which parts or growths are superposed or densely stacked.

senses.definition: A riding animal or other thing used as a mount.
senses.usage_conditions: A noun for something ridden, especially an animal designated or fit for riding.

senses.definition: Traveling or transport camels used as riding mounts.
senses.usage_conditions: A collective noun for camels on which people journey or which carry goods; it has no ordinary singular in this usage.
A plural or collective designation for people who are riding rather than traveling on foot.

senses.definition: A company of mounted travelers; a caravan.
senses.usage_conditions: A collective noun for a group of riders or travelers, commonly camels or a mixed mounted company.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be upon, overlie, overlay, or become superincumbent upon something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive or passive construction describing one thing coming upon or remaining over another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lie in layers, one part upon or over another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of fat disposed in successive layers; the broader layering construction is also expressed by related derived forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come upon, overtake, or follow closely after someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used with a person's track or road for following immediately behind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To travel along or upon a road, sand, desert, or sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction for taking a route or voyaging upon the sea; it may also describe venturing into a difficult circumstance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To venture upon, undertake, encounter, or master an affair or difficulty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with an affair, the night, fear, or another demanding matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commit a sin, crime, or comparable wrongful act.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional figurative transitive use with an offense or wrongdoing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do an evil, harmful, or abominable act to someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction رَكِبَهُ بِمَكْرُوهٍ and related expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become heavily indebted; for debt to burden someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used both of incurring much debt and of debt coming upon or weighing upon a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go at random, heedlessly, or headlong, without a settled direction or guide.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of following one's own opinion or desire without deliberation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To adhere to another's state, way, or manner of acting and do as that person does.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic construction describing conformity to another's conduct or way.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For fever or a similar affliction to continue upon or beset someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use for an illness remaining upon a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike someone with the knee or strike the person's knee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction can describe taking someone by the hair and striking the forehead with the knee.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer a complaint or ailment of the knee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-form expression with neuter significance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be large in the knee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a person or animal with an unusually large knee.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lend or mount a person on a horse for an expedition in return for an agreed share of the spoil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expeditionary arrangement in which the rider receives part of the spoil.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove a shoot from one place and plant it in another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a palm-tree shoot being transplanted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a colt or young animal to become fit for riding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes reaching the suitable age or condition for being ridden.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give, appoint, or assign someone an animal to ride; to mount someone on an animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative construction may specify the rider's position or the quality of the mount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone venture upon, undertake, or commit an affair or offense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative causative construction parallel to making someone embark upon an affair or wrongdoing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become composed or constituted, with one part set upon or fixed into another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an object whose components are put together, such as a stone set in a ring or an arrowhead fixed in a shaft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To heap or pile up one above another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of clouds becoming layered or superposed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask someone to provide or assign an animal for riding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may be followed by the provider's actually assigning the mount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The pubic region or pudendum; in some descriptions, the pubic hair or adjacent lower abdominal region.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily term with recorded differences over whether it applies to men, women, or both.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whiteness on the knee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct nominal anatomical or descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single ride or act of riding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A countable noun whose plural denotes separate rides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The knee or corresponding joint of a human or quadruped.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In animal anatomy the term is applied to the relevant forelimb joint, with detailed terminology varying by species.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In an idiom, an agitating or alarming affair in which people's knees metaphorically knock together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative expression for severe disturbance or apprehension.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A knee-based comparison for things that are alike or correspondent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression likens two corresponding things to the two knees of a she-goat; related usage describes a mark resembling a knee.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a proverb, the condition of having one's fat upon the knee, signifying quick anger or perfidy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed proverbial expression whose interpretation includes being easily angered.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lower part or base of the plant called صِلِّيَانَة after it has been cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mode, manner, or act of riding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the quality or style with which someone rides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relatively small company of camel riders or camel travelers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A group designation smaller than رَكْب and conventionally associated with camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The winds that bear or carry clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative genitive expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The stirrup of a horse's saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A saddle accessory, distinct from the collective noun for riding camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel bearing gall-marks or saddle sores on its back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized descriptive use of the noun as an epithet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road or route ridden upon and made even or easier by travel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use describing a road suitable for riding or trodden smooth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fellow rider or one who rides with another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used in specialized expressions for an associate accompanying officials or collectors.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A row of palm trees planted along a watercourse or in a line.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A water channel, strip, or cultivated area between fields, gardens, or rivulets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Regional descriptions include a channel, the land between two plots, or a place of seed-produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: People who dwell beside a watercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression equivalent to residents settled by water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A term for olive oil brought from Syria by camel transport.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nisbah adjective naming the oil by its mode of transport or provenance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who rides much or is an accomplished rider.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine counterpart is used for a woman who rides much.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who repeatedly undertakes and masters affairs through knowledge, experience, and judgment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative intensive expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A nightmare or incubus that comes upon a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression عَلاهُ الرُّكَّابُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A palm shoot growing from the trunk or upper part of a palm tree without an independent root in the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A botanical term for a shoot that may remain attached to and sometimes bear with its parent tree.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The first growths emerging from the envelope of a wheat ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The head or summit of a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative topographical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rider, traditionally especially a rider on a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The unprefixed noun can have the narrower camel-rider sense, while a prefixed construction may specify a rider on another animal; its plural usages include mounted companies.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person on board a ship or boat; a voyager upon the water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural expression for ship passengers or water travelers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A streak or layer of fat overlying another in the front part of a camel's hump.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural رَوَاكِبُ denotes successive fat layers; layers in the rear are distinguished by another term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large company of camel riders or camel travelers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A group designation larger than رَكْب and associated specifically with camel travel in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place or means of riding: a mount, vessel, saddle, or other vehicle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun applies to things on, in, or upon which one is carried, including ships and boats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The principal star of Pegasus, named by reference to the place of a saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized astronomical name.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A colt or beast that has reached the age or condition at which it may be ridden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive participial noun for an animal fit for riding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man lent or given a horse for an expedition, typically in return for a share of the spoil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may also describe one who has mounted the assigned horse; a separate attested use describes weakness in horsemanship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing set or fixed in another thing; something composed or put together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Examples include a stone set in a signet ring and an arrowhead fixed in its shaft.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Origin, stock, or place of growth and germination.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In expressions concerning a person's rank, it can refer figuratively to the origin of that standing among the people.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The example is covered by the broader causative assignment or mounting construction.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form I entry.
The idiom is covered by the established random or heedless movement expression.
The nominal riding interpretation is covered by the mode or act of riding entry.
The adjectival form is covered by the established large-knee meaning.
The camel example is covered by the same large-knee adjective.
The listed mounts, vessels, saddles, and vehicles instantiate the general means-or-place-of-riding meaning.

cautions: Several Classical entries record competing analyses of the scope or gender of specialized anatomical and rider-group terms; the definitions retain the attested alternatives without imposing a single disputed restriction.
